title: Nursing and Billing Bulletin: Counting Re-Leveled Nights on an Assisted Living Respite Stay
content:
When a nurse assessment moves an Assisted Living Respite Stay under the Respite and Short-Term Stay Agreement to another care level, the re-leveled nights are counted by one of three methods. Which method applies turns on the new stay type on record, the price charged per night by the segment being re-leveled (that segment's amount divided by its nights), the check-in date, the level effective date (the assessment date) and the care points on record.

## The three counting methods

**Arrival review.** Where the new stay type on record bills a higher nightly rate than the price charged per night by the segment being re-leveled, the assessment date falls no more days after the check-in date than the arrival review window, and the care points on record exceed the highest score of the band below the new stay type by at least the band tolerance, the assessment is an arrival review and the re-leveled nights run from the check-in date through the last night of that segment, both counted, less the screened nights absorbed.

**Move to a lower rate.** Where the new stay type on record bills a lower nightly rate than the price charged per night by the segment being re-leveled, the re-leveled nights run from the night after the level effective date through the last night of that segment, both counted.

**Every other case.** In every other case the re-leveled nights run from the level effective date through the last night of that segment, both counted.

## Terms of the arrival review test

- The nightly rate the new stay type bills is its published nightly rate.
- The days after check-in are the calendar days from the check-in date to the assessment date; an assessment on the check-in date is 0 days after it.
- The highest score of the band below the new stay type is one less than the lowest care-point score the new stay type accepts: 25 points below the Assisted Living Respite Stay (Enhanced Care), whose band starts at 26, and 50 points below the Assisted Living Respite Stay (Extensive Care), whose band starts at 51. The care points exceed it by the care points on record less that score.
- All three conditions must hold together; an assessment that meets the rate condition but misses the window or the band test is counted under "every other case".

## Condition table

| New stay type's published rate against the segment's price per night | Assessment within the arrival review window after check-in | Excess over the band below at least the band tolerance | Method |
|---|---|---|---|
| Higher | Yes | Yes | Arrival review |
| Higher | Yes | No | Every other case |
| Higher | No | Yes or no | Every other case |
| Lower | Any | Any | Move to a lower rate |
| Equal | Any | Any | Every other case |

## Worked counts (hypothetical stay; the window, tolerance and absorbed nights are illustrative inputs)

The segment being re-leveled is a planned-stay segment of the Assisted Living Respite Stay (Standard Care) at 239.00 a night, first night and check-in 1 May, last night 14 May.

1. Assessment on 2 May places the guest in Enhanced Care (published rate 284.00, higher than 239.00) with 33 care points. With an arrival review window of 1 day, the assessment is 1 day after check-in, within the window; the excess over 25 is 8, at least a band tolerance of 5. Arrival review: 1 May through 14 May, both counted, is 14 nights, less 2 screened nights absorbed: 12 re-leveled nights.
2. The same assessment on 6 May is 5 days after check-in, beyond a 1-day window: every other case, 6 May through 14 May, both counted: 9 nights.
3. A stay at Enhanced Care, 284.00 a night, whose assessment on 6 May places the guest in Standard Care (239.00, lower): from 7 May through 14 May, both counted: 8 nights.
